summary: Mr. Sutton explores the historical and spiritual significance of the city of Mitzpah, the site where Gedalia was governor after the destruction of the First Beit HaMikdash. He connects the city's history from the time of Melech Asa to the actions of Yehuda HaMaccabee, illustrating how historical mistakes can be rectified through Teshuvah.
questions: Why is Mitzpah significant to the story of Gedalia?
What was the historical connection between Melech Asa and the city of Mitzpah?
How did Yehuda HaMaccabee rectify the mistakes of the past at Mitzpah?
What is the lesson of Teshuvah that can be learned from the history of Mitzpah?
